rows.name: REMOTE_HOST
rows.who_sets: A developer, for one `make` test run.
rows.values: One worker host name. More than 1 word stops `make` with an error. `make REMOTE_HOST=name` also works.
rows.effect: `make` adds `--remote-host=<value>` to the `bin/slice run` command of the targets `test`, `test-core`, `test-host`, `test-fpga` and `test-fast`. Slice then pins the remote run to that worker host.
rows.notes: It needs the remote mode `1`, `sku0` or `sku1` (the value of `REMOTE`). With the mode `0`, `make` stops with an error for every goal. `TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION` supplies a mode only for build goals and test goals. The remote build job does not receive it.

evidence.quote: $(error REMOTE_HOST accepts exactly one worker hostname)

rows.name: REMOTE_MODEL
rows.who_sets: A developer, for one `make` test run.
rows.values: One CPU model name that OpenLava (the LSF scheduler of the FPGA worker pool) knows. More than 1 word stops `make`. `make REMOTE_MODEL=name` also works.
rows.effect: `make` adds `--remote-model=<value>` to the `bin/slice run` command of the targets `test`, `test-core`, `test-host`, `test-fpga` and `test-fast`. Slice then requires that CPU model for the remote run.
rows.notes: It needs the remote mode `1` (the value of `REMOTE`). With the mode `0`, `make` stops with an error for every goal. With `sku0` or `sku1`, `make` stops with the error `already selects a pool class`. The remote build job does not receive it.

evidence.quote: $(error REMOTE_MODEL accepts exactly one OpenLava model name)
$(error $(REMOTE_MODE_SOURCE)=$(REMOTE_MODE) already selects a pool class; omit REMOTE_MODEL)

rows.name: REMOTE_PREFER
rows.who_sets: Nothing in the repository. `GNUmakefile` rejects it.
rows.values: Any text that is not blank. The text is not parsed. `make REMOTE_PREFER=value` has the same effect.
rows.effect: `make` stops for every goal with the error `REMOTE_REQUIRE and REMOTE_PREFER are not supported`.
rows.notes: `GNUmakefile` only tests that the value is not blank. The error text names the supported inputs: `REMOTE=sku0`, `REMOTE=sku1`, `REMOTE_MODEL` and `REMOTE_HOST`.

evidence.quote: $(error REMOTE_REQUIRE and REMOTE_PREFER are not supported; use REMOTE=sku0, REMOTE=sku1, REMOTE_MODEL, or REMOTE_HOST)

rows.name: REMOTE_REQUIRE
rows.who_sets: Nothing in the repository. `GNUmakefile` rejects it.
rows.values: Any text that is not blank. The text is not parsed. `make REMOTE_REQUIRE=value` has the same effect.
rows.effect: `make` stops for every goal with the error `REMOTE_REQUIRE and REMOTE_PREFER are not supported`.
rows.notes: `GNUmakefile` only tests that the value is not blank. The error text names the supported inputs: `REMOTE=sku0`, `REMOTE=sku1`, `REMOTE_MODEL` and `REMOTE_HOST`.

evidence.quote: $(error REMOTE_REQUIRE and REMOTE_PREFER are not supported; use REMOTE=sku0, REMOTE=sku1, REMOTE_MODEL, or REMOTE_HOST)

rows.name: REMOVE_GLOBAL
rows.who_sets: Nothing. The script sets it for the option `--remove-global`.
rows.values: Any text that is not empty. The text is not parsed.
rows.default: Unset: the script continues with its normal Rust check.
rows.effect: The script acts as if `--remove-global` was given. Without root rights it prints an error and exits with code 1. As root it removes the apt packages `rustc`, `cargo` and `librust-std*` when `dpkg` reports a `rustc` package, and then exits with code 0.
rows.notes: The script does not clear the variable at its start. CMake runs the script at configure time. With a value in the environment, a configure by a normal user fails with `Failed to set up Rust`. As root, the configure removes the apt Rust packages.

rows.name: TOKENIZER_PYTHON_VERSION
rows.who_sets: CI workflow `publish-deb.yml`, on the `make` command line.
rows.values: A Python version that `uv --python` accepts, for example `3.12.7`. `make` does not check the text.
rows.default: Unset: `3.12.7`. Empty: `make` keeps the empty text and passes no version to `uv`.
rows.effect: When `IN_NIX_SHELL` is empty, `make` passes it to `uv` as `--python <value>` in `make tokenize-deps` and in the PyInstaller build of `gen/tokenize_py` (the packaged tokenizer executable). That executable embeds this Python interpreter. A changed value makes `make` build `gen/tokenize_py` again.
rows.notes: It is also the default of `INGEST_PYTHON_VERSION`. When `IN_NIX_SHELL` is not empty, the recipes do not run `uv`, and `gen/tokenize_py` is a copy of the file that `TRON_TOKENIZE_PY` names. `make TOKENIZER_PYTHON_VERSION=version` also works.

rows.name: TRON_FEATURE_BRANCH_BUILD
rows.who_sets: CI workflow `publish-deb.yml`, with `1` on feature branches.
rows.values: Any text that is not empty turns it on. The text is not parsed. `0` and `false` also turn it on.
rows.default: Unset: off. The version is the exact tag of `HEAD`, the `git describe` text on a `release-*` branch, or the date and the commit hash.
rows.effect: On a named branch other than `main` and `release-*`, `bin/get-version.sh` prints `<tag without v>+feature.<branch>.<commits since the tag>.g<8-character commit hash>`. The tag is the nearest reachable tag that matches `v[0-9]*`. The script exits with code 1 when no such tag exists or the tag does not have the version form.
rows.notes: The version form is `v<numbers with dots>` plus an optional `-devN`, `-tcN` or `-rcN`. The variable has no effect on `main`, on `release-*` branches and on a detached `HEAD`. `bin/make-version.sh` and `bin/get-deb-version.sh` use the printed version for the compiled programs and the Debian package.

rows.name: TRON_HOME_ROOT
rows.who_sets: Nothing in the repository sets it.
rows.values: Path of the directory that holds the home directories. The script compares it as text with the physical path of `HOME`.
rows.effect: `bin/scratch-dir.sh` creates a build directory below `TRON_SCRATCH_USERS` only when the physical path of `HOME` is below this directory and the checkout is below `HOME`. The part of the `HOME` path after this directory names the user folder below `TRON_SCRATCH_USERS`.
rows.notes: A value with a trailing slash never matches. The script does not resolve symbolic links in the value. When the comparison fails, a new build directory is a plain directory in the checkout. `GNUmakefile` runs the script.

rows.name: TRON_HOST_MIN_TRON
rows.who_sets: A developer who builds `tron-host` for another apt channel.
rows.values: A Debian package version, for example `2.0.0~1tc6` or `2026.07.01-2ebdc1e8`. The text is not checked. `make TRON_HOST_MIN_TRON=version` also works.
rows.default: Unset: `2.0.0~1tc6`. Empty: `packaging/tron-host/build-deb.sh` receives 2 arguments in place of 3 and exits with code 2.
rows.effect: `make deb-host` passes the value to `packaging/tron-host/build-deb.sh`. The script writes `Depends: tron (>= <value>)` into the control file of the `tron-host` package. The value is the oldest `tron` package version that `tron-host` accepts.
rows.notes: Only the target `deb-host` uses it. `tron-host` is the optional package that holds `rinzler_host` (a rinzler build that serves models on the CPU and needs no FPGA card).

rows.name: TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE
rows.who_sets: A developer with a prebuilt bundle. The Nix test build exports it.
rows.values: Path of a plugin bundle (a directory with a `manifest.json` file and generated model plugin headers). The text is used as written. `make TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE=path` also works.
rows.default: Unset: no bundle. `make` passes an empty value to CMake, and the build generates the plugin headers with ingest.
rows.effect: For the configure targets `gen/config/core`, `gen/config/dev`, `gen/config/test` and `gen/config/prod`, `make` passes the path to CMake as `-DTRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE`. CMake verifies the bundle and copies the plugin headers from it, and ingest does not run. A changed value makes `make` run the CMake configure again.
rows.notes: `make deb` ignores it and passes an empty value. `make deb-host` does not pass it. CMake does not read the environment variable. A direct `cmake` run needs the option `-DTRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE=path`.

rows.name: TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STAMP
rows.values: Path of the stamp file (a file whose change makes `make` repeat a step). The text is used as written. `make TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STAMP=path` also works.
rows.default: Unset: `gen/.ingest_plugin_bundle_stamp`. Empty: the stamp helper fails, and `make` stops with `Failed to update` for goals that update the stamp.
rows.effect: The stamp helper (`bin/ci/update-ingest-plugin-bundle-stamp.sh`) writes the value of `TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE` and a newline into this file when the content differs. The targets `gen/config/core`, `gen/config/dev`, `gen/config/test` and `gen/config/prod` depend on the file. A changed file makes `make` run the CMake configure again.
rows.notes: The helper creates the parent directory. The helper exits with an error when the path is a symbolic link, or exists and is not a regular file. `make` then stops with `Failed to update <path>`.

rows.name: TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STAMP_HELPER
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `GNUmakefile` assigns it and exports it to its recipes and to nested `make` runs.
rows.values: Path of the program that updates the file that `TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STAMP` names. `make` does not use a value from the environment. `make TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STAMP_HELPER=path` replaces the program.
rows.effect: A value in the environment has no effect. `GNUmakefile` assigns the fixed path with `:=`. `make` runs that program while it reads the makefile, and the targets `gen/config/core`, `gen/config/dev`, `gen/config/test` and `gen/config/prod` depend on the file.
rows.notes: With `make -e` the environment value replaces the assignment of the makefile. No script in the checkout reads the exported variable.

rows.name: TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STAMP_REQUIRED
rows.values: Only the text `1` turns the stamp update on. Any other text counts as off.
rows.default: Unset: `make` sets `1` when no goal is given, or when a goal is outside its list of goals that do not use the bundle.
rows.effect: With `1`, `make` runs the stamp helper (`bin/ci/update-ingest-plugin-bundle-stamp.sh`) while it reads the makefile. A value of `1` in the environment turns the stamp update on for the goals that skip it, for example `clean`, `lint` and `deb`.
rows.notes: It is an internal variable of `GNUmakefile`. For all other goals `make` assigns `1` and does not use an environment value. A command-line assignment replaces the value for every goal. `make` does not read it when the only goals are `list-tests` or `list-tests-core`.

rows.name: TRON_NIX_RUST_TOOLCHAIN
rows.who_sets: `flake.nix`, in the Nix dev shells and the Nix checks.
rows.values: Path of a Rust toolchain directory. `rust/run-cargo` requires the executable files `bin/cargo`, `bin/rustc`, `bin/rustdoc` and `bin/rustfmt` in it.
rows.default: Unset: no effect when `IN_NIX_SHELL` is empty. When `IN_NIX_SHELL` is not empty, `rust/run-cargo` and `rust/rust-toolchain.sh` stop with an error.
rows.effect: The scripts read it only when `IN_NIX_SHELL` is not empty. `rust/run-cargo` runs `<value>/bin/cargo` and points cargo at the `rustc`, `rustdoc` and `rustfmt` of that directory. `rust/rust-toolchain.sh` checks that `rustc` and `cargo` on `PATH` are the same files as in `<value>/bin`.
rows.notes: `rust/rust-toolchain.sh` also requires that this `rustc` has the version in `rust-toolchain.toml`. `flake.nix` sets the variable in the Nix dev shells, in the lint shell, in its `lefthook` wrapper and in its checks.

evidence.quote: : "${TRON_NIX_RUST_TOOLCHAIN:?Nix shell did not declare its Rust toolchain}"

rows.name: TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION
rows.who_sets: The shell profile of a shared development machine.
rows.values: Exactly one of `0`, `1`, `sku0`, `sku1`. `sku0` and `sku1` each select one CPU model of the worker pool. Other text stops `make` when the value is used.
rows.default: Unset: `0` (local). Empty: `make` stops with an error for build goals and test goals when `REMOTE` is not defined.
rows.effect: `make` copies it to `REMOTE` when `REMOTE` is not defined and the goals include a build goal or a test goal. A bare `make` counts as the build goal `all`. With `1`, `sku0` or `sku1`, `make` submits builds to an LSF worker and runs the Slice test targets with `--remote`.
rows.notes: `REMOTE` from the command line or the environment overrides it. Goals such as `lint` ignore it. With `1`, `sku0` or `sku1`, goals that run tests without Slice stop with an error, for example `test-proxy`. `make TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION=1` also works.

evidence.quote: $(error $(REMOTE_MODE_SOURCE) must be one of 0, 1, sku0, or sku1)

rows.name: TRON_SCRATCH_USERS
rows.who_sets: Nothing in the repository sets it.
rows.values: Path of the directory under which each user has a folder for build output.
rows.effect: For each build directory, `bin/scratch-dir.sh` creates `<value>/<HOME below TRON_HOME_ROOT>/tmp/<checkout path below HOME>/<directory>` and puts a symbolic link to it in the checkout. The build directories are `gen`, `gen-deb`, `gen-deb-host`, `gen-tsan`, `gen-asan` and `gen-coverage`.
rows.notes: A new build directory is a plain directory in the checkout in 5 cases: `CI` is not empty, `HOME` is not below `TRON_HOME_ROOT`, the checkout is not below `HOME`, `cmake` is missing or older than version 3.24, or the script cannot create the directory.

evidence.quote: SCRATCH_DIRS := gen gen-deb gen-deb-host gen-tsan gen-asan gen-coverage

rows.name: USER_INSTALL
rows.who_sets: Nothing. The script sets it for the option `--user`.
rows.values: Any text that is not empty. The text is not parsed.
rows.default: Unset: the script continues with its normal Rust check.
rows.effect: The script acts as if `--user` was given. It installs Rust in `$HOME/.cargo` when none exists, or upgrades the Rust there when its version differs from `rust-toolchain.toml`. Then it exits and does not write `rust/rustenv` (the file that tells `rust/run-cargo` which Rust to use outside Nix).
rows.notes: The script does not clear the variable at its start. CMake runs the script at configure time. A value in the environment therefore also applies to a CMake configure. The script tests `REMOVE_GLOBAL` first.

rows.name: __NIX_USERNAME
rows.who_sets: The Nix dev shell hook. No person sets it.
rows.read_by: The shell hook of the Nix dev shell (`flake.nix`)
rows.values: A user name. On x86_64 Linux the hook sets it from `id -un` and replaces a value from the caller.
rows.default: Unset: the hook sets it on x86_64 Linux. On other systems the hook does not use it.
rows.effect: The hook stores the output of `id -un` in it at its start. At its end the hook puts `(nix) ` before the prompt text `PS1` and replaces `\u` in `PS1` with the name. Then the hook unsets the variable.
rows.notes: It is a temporary variable of the hook. The hook exports it, and programs that the hook starts receive it. When `id -un` prints nothing, the hook does not change `PS1`, and the variable stays set and empty.

new_terms.definition: The value of the Make variable `REMOTE`. `0` runs builds and tests on the local machine. `1`, `sku0` and `sku1` send them to the worker pool.
The servers that LSF gives remote builds and remote test runs to.
The LSF scheduler of the FPGA worker pool. Distributed Dice submits remote test runs to it.
A directory with a `manifest.json` file and the model plugin headers that an earlier ingest run generated. A build can copy the headers from it in place of running ingest.
A small file that holds the value of a build input. When its content changes, `make` repeats the step that depends on it.
The script `bin/ci/update-ingest-plugin-bundle-stamp.sh`. It writes the path of the selected plugin bundle into the stamp file.
The Make targets `gen/config/core`, `gen/config/dev`, `gen/config/test` and `gen/config/prod`. Each one runs the CMake configure step for one build profile.
The optional Debian package that holds `rinzler_host`. `make deb-host` builds it.
A rinzler build that serves models on the CPU and needs no FPGA card.
The file that `rust/rust-toolchain.sh` writes. `rust/run-cargo` reads it outside Nix to find the Rust installation.
The tokenizer executable that the `tron` package ships. Outside Nix, PyInstaller builds it with an embedded Python interpreter.

notes: All 18 variables have a row and none is dropped. TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STAMP_HELPER has no reader of the environment value. It stays in the list: GNUmakefile exports it to recipe environments. TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STAMP_REQUIRED is an internal Make variable. It stays in the list: the environment supplies it for goals where GNUmakefile does not assign it. __NIX_USERNAME is a temporary exported variable of the Nix dev shell hook. REMOVE_GLOBAL and USER_INSTALL are uninitialized shell variables of rust/rust-toolchain.sh. An environment value acts as the matching command-line option, also when CMake runs the script. Group choices: the two rust/rust-toolchain.sh variables are in cmake (CMake runs that script at configure time), the four TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE names are in ingest-build, TRON_HOST_MIN_TRON and TRON_FEATURE_BRANCH_BUILD are in packaging. Five evidence quotes are an exact part of the line, not the whole line. Three of these lines are in GNUmakefile and are longer than 120 characters. One line of bin/scratch-dir.sh and one line of flake.nix hold a pipe character. Statements about an empty value of a '?=' variable and about 'make -e' rest on GNU Make rules, not on a line of the checkout. doc/slice.md says build goals ignore TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION. GNUmakefile applies it to build goals. The row follows GNUmakefile.
